answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, transferable stake before it may bid for work, with the stake held by an independent escrow contract. After a job, randomly selected peers verify the result against a public rubric; proven fraud triggers a challenge and slashes the stake, while honest agents recover it. Spawning a hundred sybils therefore means tying up a hundred stakes and risking each one, not merely minting names. The cost rises like a terrace above an ocean: each extra identity must climb the same ridge of capital and exposure.
